In summary, our research is concerned with
a better characterization of interstellar dust in the direction of Cyg X2 and with the first spatially resolved study of the dust halo around an X-ray binary source.
the dust and gas components of the ISM, which can be studied in detail only by X-ray observations of bright sources.
the interplay of the X-ray source emission, dust absorption, and scattering.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
we cannot exclude the presence of oxygen in either of the proposed forms, but we cannot prove the presence of one of these forms either.
the ISM absorption in Cyg X- 2 is due to a mixture of ionized and molecular oxygen, and that a substantial part of oxygen is locked in the silicate grains.
the dust is distributed smoothly toward the source and that the dust is composed of silicate grains, which are responsible for a substantial part of the absorption of the source emission.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have detected and analyzed for the first time a scattering halo and its spectral properties, which are consistent with a silicate-dominated dust.
we have detected the presence of dust grains in the ISM, which are responsible for the scattering of the X-rays and for absorption by the elements present in dust.
, in this observation of Cyg X-2 with XMM-Newton, the interstellar dust along the line of  sight to the source is well characterized.
The main takeaway from our work is that
X-ray observations of scattering halos can be used to investigate the dust properties in the ISM.
X-ray spectroscopy of the halo can be used to investigate dust absorption in the ISM.
the EPIC-pN data can be used to constrain the dust size distribution and its spatial distribution.
